=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py: lines 3040-3052 (`_inject_token_into_url`), lines 3055-3085 (`_resolve_origin_url`) | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: Git authentication was moved from per-process `http.extraHeader` to embedding `GH_TOKEN` directly in clone URLs.
  WHY: Tokens become visible in process arguments, Git diagnostics, and persisted `.git/config` remotes, violating credential hygiene and breaking authenticated subprocess operations.

- scripts/memory_helpers.sh: lines 137-183 (`_memory_ensure_branch`), lines 569-585 (`_memory_force_tick_remote_url`), lines 624-630 / 767 / 883 / 919 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: Memory helpers embed credentials in remote URLs and replace authenticated `_memory_git` calls with bare Git commands.
  WHY: Tokens leak through argv and persisted remotes, while workflows using `persist-credentials: false` lose authentication and memory branch operations fail or silently do not persist.

- scripts/targeted_file_context.py: lines 152-172 (deleted), lines 240-247 (`normalize_path`), lines 568-579 (`emit_context`) | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: Sensitive-path filtering, path normalization, and path-count/byte limits were removed, and `emit_context` iterates raw paths.
  WHY: Untrusted targets can read credential-bearing files into model context, creating an exfiltration channel and allowing unbounded prompt output.

- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh: lines 48-51, lines 210-215, line 664 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: The diagnose phase bypasses the model-provider broker and changes from read-only execution to `--sandbox danger-full-access`.
  WHY: Issue-derived diagnostics are processed with ambient provider credentials and workspace write/command/network access, violating the documented isolation boundary.

- scripts/codex_helpers.sh: lines 135-476 (deleted `model_provider_broker_*` functions) | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: The model-provider broker helper family was deleted while production scripts and workflows still invoke it.
  WHY: Model-facing phases abort with undefined-function errors under `set -e` before launching Codex, including the review/autofix pipeline.

- scripts/gh_helpers.sh: lines 493-498 (deleted `git_with_github_auth`), lines 947-1352 (deleted `review_blocked_*` family) | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: Git authentication and review-blocked terminal-decision helpers were deleted while existing judges and orchestrator code still call them.
  WHY: Review-blocked pushes and approval/successor flows fail with command-not-found or unauthenticated Git errors and can stall permanently.

- scripts/write_codex_config.sh: lines 95-110 (option parser), lines 143-148, lines 258-264 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: `--provider-base-url` was removed and the base URL is hardcoded to the public OpenRouter endpoint.
  WHY: Existing broker-routed callers fail with an unknown argument, while any successful configuration bypasses the loopback broker.

- scripts/codex_helpers.sh: lines 52-145 (`codex_config_assemble`) | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: `codex_config_assemble` no longer accepts or forwards `--provider-base-url`.
  WHY: Broker-routed callers fail during argument parsing or lose the broker endpoint.

- scripts/gh_helpers.sh: lines 766-780 (REST projection), lines 833-839 (GraphQL projection), lines 913-924 (jq mapper) | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: Comment projections drop `id`, `author_id`, `author_type`, and `author_association`.
  WHY: Review-blocked producer-marker and maintainer-approval authentication cannot identify valid requests or approvals on either GraphQL or REST paths.

- scripts/codex_stall_guard.sh: lines 404-407 (`_signal_child_group`), lines 439-444 (`_kill_child_group_if_running`), lines 560-563 (idle SIGKILL gate) | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: The guard returns early after the tracked `sudo` wrapper exits and therefore skips privileged signalling of surviving isolated-group members.
  WHY: A nobody-owned editor can survive after its wrapper exits, reproducing the mixed-ownership signal gap that issue #4075 is intended to fix.

- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh: lines 292-332 (`terminate_editor_attempt_process_group`), lines 2178 and 2200 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: Missing metadata/helper or privileged-signal failures only kill the runner-owned guard, while watchdog calls use `|| true`.
  WHY: The isolated editor group can remain alive while cleanup proceeds or exits, leaving the original signal gap and potentially racing workspace ownership restoration.

- tests/test_targeted_file_context.py: lines 30 and 37 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: Tests still import deleted `MAX_TARGET_PATHS` and `is_sensitive_target_path` symbols.
  WHY: Pytest collection raises `ImportError` before the targeted-context tests execute.

- scripts/targeted_file_context.py: lines 562-564 (`emit_context`) | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `max_bytes=0` now returns a header and disabled marker instead of an empty string.
  WHY: The documented disable-switch contract and existing tests fail, causing callers to receive non-empty targeted context.

- scripts/targeted_file_context.py: lines 564-579, lines 562-713 (`emit_context`) | severity=major | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: Missing-file, binary, and wrapper output is not fully charged against `used_bytes`, and the path-count cap is removed.
  WHY: Large invalid-path lists can produce output beyond `max_bytes`, defeating the prompt-size limit.

- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh: lines 59-68 | severity=major | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: Cleanup changed from a `HEAD` tree check with staged restoration and cached-file removal to an index-only check and worktree-only restore.
  WHY: Staged or tracked `pre_assembled_static.txt` can be deleted, retained, or included incorrectly in implementation commits.

- scripts/editor_isolation_preflight.sh: lines 145-159 (`editor_isolation_signal_process_group`) | severity=nit | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: Unexpected `pgrep` errors are treated as an empty process group after a failed privileged kill.
  WHY: A transient `/proc` error can falsely report successful signalling and skip escalation.

- scripts/codex_stall_guard.sh: lines 187-203 (`_isolated_user_from_command`) | severity=major | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Invalid isolation usernames or lookup failures silently disable privileged signalling.
  WHY: The guard falls back to a runner-owned signal path that cannot kill nobody-owned processes without an operator-visible diagnostic.

- scripts/codex_stall_guard.sh: lines 415-416 (post-sudo success path) | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Successful `sudo -n kill` is accepted without immediately verifying that isolated-group members disappeared.
  WHY: A policy or pgid mismatch can make signal delivery ineffective while individual forwarded signals remain unverified.

- scripts/editor_isolation_preflight.sh: lines 162-179 (`editor_isolation_verify_process_group_stopped`) | severity=major | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Transient `pgrep` failures are treated as metadata/cleanup failure rather than retried inspection errors.
  WHY: A recoverable `/proc` failure can abort cleanup and leave workspace ownership unrestored.

- scripts/codex_stall_guard.sh: lines 270-296 (`_write_process_group_metadata`) | severity=nit | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The metadata directory's permissions are not explicitly verified as restrictive.
  WHY: A permissive parent directory can expose the privileged signal target to another process.

- scripts/codex_stall_guard.sh: lines 270-296 (`_write_process_group_metadata`) | severity=nit | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Cross-filesystem `os.replace` failures receive only a generic error.
  WHY: The operation fails closed but gives insufficient diagnostic detail when configured runtime paths span filesystems.

- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh: lines 263-281 (`cleanup_editor_isolation`) | severity=nit | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Invalid `EDITOR_ISOLATION_KILL_VERIFY_ATTEMPTS` values silently fall back to 20.
  WHY: Operator misconfiguration is hidden and may cause cleanup to report failure under a too-short effective timeout.

- scripts/codex_stall_guard.sh: lines 384-394 (`_verify_isolated_group_stopped`) | severity=nit | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Verification performs up to 20 sequential `pgrep` subprocesses at 100 ms intervals for every escalation.
  WHY: Repeated polling adds avoidable latency and resource use, especially across retries.

- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh: lines 292-332 (`terminate_editor_attempt_process_group`) | severity=nit | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The function unconditionally sleeps 5 seconds after a successful TERM before checking whether KILL is needed.
  WHY: Clean editor exits incur unnecessary wall-clock latency that compounds with verification polling.

- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh: lines 147-149 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: `patch_diagnose_reasoning_into_config` now writes `~/.codex/config.toml` even on the `handled=false` early-return path.
  WHY: The diagnose phase mutates configuration on a path that previously should only synthesize a result.

- scripts/editor_isolation_preflight.sh: lines 156-159 (`editor_isolation_signal_process_group`) | severity=nit | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: After a failed privileged kill, any nonzero `pgrep` result is treated as confirmation that no processes remain.
  WHY: Inspection errors are indistinguishable from an empty group, so KILL escalation can be ski
